summary: The article's lead states that DPP Shalimar Hack, while defending the charges, "publicly stated that the vessel's navigational and safety systems were defective." This is the reporter's characterisation — the article contains NO direct quotation of the DPP using the word 'defective' or describing the systems, and no other outlet carries this line. The DPP's stated basis: "The decision to do so was based upon careful consideration of the evidence presented, the relevant principles of law involved, case law authorities from the United Kingdom, Commonwealth jurisdictions, the European Court of Human Rights, and.

Andrew Donald, who says he commanded the MV Barima during 12 years at the Transport & Harbours Department, describes the vessel as "a floating disaster waiting to occur" and states "I blame T&HD and its subject ministers." No other outlet in this survey carries Donald. Donald "described the MV Barima as a single-hull passenger vessel and alleged that it operated contrary to standards contained in the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea." HGPTV immediately qualifies: "Whether those specific international requirements applied to the vessel and whether it complied with the relevant domestic rules.

Nigel Hughes described the murder charges as a "most perverse attempt at distraction" and questioned whether the allegations were supported by evidence of the intent legally required for murder. Hughes on the mens rea: "A charge of murder requires that the accused had the intention to kill his victim." He argued the prosecution "would have to establish that the accused possessed that intention when the vessel departed or developed it at some point during the voyage." Hughes on the COI effect: "Could it be that the real intention here is [that], the accused having been charged with murder, would not be able to.

States the three accused were charged with "72 counts of murder" — the first HGPTV statement of a count. The article does NOT explain how the 72 counts are distributed among the three accused or what each corresponds to. Dr Dexter Todd is identified as representing Captain Kevin Price, Chief Mate Rondell Roberts and Goods Superintendent Delon Granderson. Todd: "How can you charge men with murder based on overloading when you do not even have an accurate calculation of the cargo weight or a completed manifest?"

RESOLVES THE COUNT. Dexter Todd, quoted directly: "We know so far that the disclosure is that 72 bodies were recovered and so they were charged for all 72 of those deaths." This is the only explanation in any source surveyed of what the 72 counts correspond to — one count per recovered body, on the prosecution's disclosure as relayed by defence counsel. "Police charged 40-year-old captain Kevin Price, 42-year-old chief mate Rondell Dwayne Roberts, and 33-year-old Delon Granderson, the loading superintendent at the Transport and Harbours Department, with a total of 72 counts of murder." The 72 is a joint total.

"Police slapped 40-year-old captain Kevin Price, 42-year-old chief mate Rondell Dwayne Roberts and 33-year-old Delon Granderson, the loading superintendent from the Transport and Harbours Department, with a total of 72 murder charges." — independent CMC confirmation of the 72 total. Gives the toll as "at least 73 people dead and more than 30 others missing and feared dead" — i.e. 72 counts against 73 confirmed dead. "Three senior crew members of MV Barima have been arrested following an indictment of 72 counts of murder" — third independent statement of the 72 figure. The article does not explain the distribution. Gives figures: "76 people have been rescued, while 73 bodies have been recovered. Out of these, 68 victims have been identified with the majority sent to their families for proper burials." — NOTE this contradicts the archive's 69 identified (24 July) and the 5-unidentified figure from iNews/Kaieteur on 28-29 July (which implies 68 identified of 73). Confirms names/ages: Captain Kevin Price 40, Chief Mate Rondell.

"Three individuals connected to the MV Barima ferry disaster have been remanded to prison following Guyana Police filing 72 murder charges related to the July 18 maritime tragedy" — fourth independent statement of the 72 figure, dated 28 July, the earliest surveyed. Names and ages consistent with all other outlets: Kevin Price 40; Rondell Dwayne Roberts 42; Delon Granderson 33, described as "Transport and Harbours Department loading official." "The charges were formally presented, though the men were not required to enter pleas due to the indictable nature of the offences. The case was transferred to Charity.

[ALLEGATION — assertion by an accused person, untested] Price, quoted verbatim: "The vessel had a lot of issues, the vessel anchor ain't wuking, the vessel radar, we don't have a radar, the vessel don't have a search and rescue transponder, the vessel don't have an EPIRB." This is the fullest published list of alleged equipment defects. [ALLEGATION — assertion by an accused person] On life rafts: "Those life rafts expired since 2022, and Maritime did an inspection and did not write off that vessel." This directly implicates MARAD's inspection regime and is the first published allegation of its kind from an.

A letter to the editor answering Nigel Hughes's intent argument directly, though without naming him: "The proposition that a charge of murder can only arise where it is proven that an accused person intended to kill or intended to inflict grievous bodily harm, knowing that death was the likely consequence is, at best, incomplete and, at worst, misleading." Argues for extreme-recklessness murder: "Where it can be established beyond a reasonable doubt that an individual acted with extreme recklessness or what is often described as a 'depraved indifference' or 'wanton disregard' for human life, the requisite mental.

POSITION SHIFT: after Opposition Leader Azruddin Mohamed offered to independently fund salvage, "the government announced that victims' families will make the final decision on whether to raise the vessel or designate the wreckage as a memorial site." This qualifies the PM's 28 July "likely to remain there as is" already in the archive. Mohamed called the prospect of leaving the vessel on the seafloor "premature and wicked" and "an act of cruelty" to grieving families. Mohamed: "families have reached out to me saying they want the bodies of their loved ones, even if all that remain are bones."

Christopher Ram, in an open letter to President Ali, argues the COI's Terms of Reference "concentrate almost exclusively on what happened during the July 18 voyage, while sidestepping the government's policy decisions leading up to the tragedy." Ram: "Your commission will inquire exhaustively into a voyage without asking why that voyage was made in that vessel at all." [NEW FACT TO THE ARCHIVE] Ram states "the newly acquired MV Kalliopi N arrived in Guyana in May and had been designated by Public Works Minister Juan Edghill for the Region One route. PM Phillips "stated on Tuesday that international salvage companies were prepared to raise the ferry MV Barima, which likely contains additional remains and investigative evidence" — i.e. the government acknowledges capability exists and that evidence is inside, while deferring to families. Phillips's substitute for physical evidence of engine failure: "the crew, the people on board could say whether the engine stopped running and they had to do any repairs." This is materially significant given that the three men best placed to say so are now remanded on murder charges. Confirms the families' consultation is a.

"The murder prosecution arising from the MV Barima tragedy does not have to await the findings of the Commission of Inquiry, the Director of Public Prosecutions has said amid mounting criticism over the charges." CRITICAL NEGATIVE FINDING: "The statement did not disclose the evidence contained in the police file or explain publicly how prosecutors intend to establish the legal elements required for murder. Those details are expected to emerge through the court proceedings." This corroborates Chabrol's observation that intent and malice went unaddressed. The DPP's cited precedents are "the 2018 Berbice piracy.

CRITICAL: this appears to be the DPP's press statement reproduced at near-full length, and it contains NO reference to the vessel's navigational or safety systems being defective. It therefore does not corroborate the Demerara Waves lead. Verbatim from the statement: "the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions reviewed a file in relation to the MV Barima tragedy of the investigations done by the Guyana Police Force in relation thereto, and duly advised the institution of the charges of murder against the Captain of the vessel Kevin Price, Chief Mate, Rondel Dwayne Roberts, and the Goods Superintendent of.

Gives 'Meadow Grove Public Road' for Roberts, agreeing with Kaieteur's 28 July report and HGPTV, against Demerara Waves and Kaieteur's 29 July report which give 'Grove Public Road'. Procedure: appeared before Chief Magistrate Judy Latchman at Georgetown Magistrates'.

However, those closely involved in the recovery operation explained that when they tried to pull the vessel, the cables and ropes kept bursting." This is the first published mechanical account of why the righting attempts failed. "Since they arrived in Guyana on Monday, July 20, the team from the French Guiana Army has executed approximately 15 diving operations to the sunken vessel."
